question: What is the exit load for the ELSS fund and why was I charged it?
expected_fee_points: definition of exit load (charged only when redeeming inside the scheme's exit-load period)
ELSS units cannot be redeemed during the lock-in, so no exit load applies
a deduction is more likely stamp duty (0.005% on purchase) or STT (0.001% on equity-fund redemption)

evidence.text: Units cannot be redeemed during the lock-in, so ELSS funds do not need an exit load.
a stamp duty of 0.005% applies when you buy mutual fund units
levied on the sale (redemption) of units at 0.001%

premise_check: The user assumes an exit load was charged; for ELSS the exit load is 0%, so the answer must correct the premise rather than invent a charge.
reference_answer: The Edelweiss ELSS Tax Saver Fund has no exit load (0%); instead, units are locked in for 3 years.
Factsheet: exit load 0%, lock-in 3 years from allotment, applied separately to each SIP instalment.
An exit load is charged only when units are redeemed inside a scheme's exit-load period; ELSS units cannot be redeemed during the lock-in.
A deduction is more likely stamp duty (0.005% on purchase, e.g. ₹0.50 on ₹10,000) or STT (0.001% on equity-fund redemption).
Check your account statement: match the deduction to a purchase (stamp duty) or a redemption (STT) and its date.
Sources: Edelweiss ELSS Tax Saver Fund Direct Growth (INDmoney); Fee Explainer – Exit load, ELSS lock-in, Stamp duty.

question: I redeemed my Flexi Cap units 8 months after buying. What exit load applies and how is it calculated?

scenario.note: 8 months is about 243 days, well past the 90-day window.

expected_facts: Flexi Cap exit load is 1% if redeemed within 0-90 days
expected_fee_points: exit load = % of NAV on units redeemed inside the period
units held 8 months are outside the 90-day window, so no exit load applies
worked example: 1% at NAV ₹100 means ₹99 per unit inside the window

evidence.text: Exit Load of 1% if redeemed in 0-90 Days
Units held past the period are redeemed with no exit load.
levied on the sale (redemption) of units at 0.001%

premise_check: At 8 months the 90-day window has passed, so the expected exit load is nil.
reference_answer: No exit load applies: you redeemed after about 8 months, past the Flexi Cap fund's 90-day exit-load window.
Factsheet: exit load of 1% if redeemed in 0-90 days; nil after that. No lock-in.
An exit load is a percentage of NAV deducted only on units redeemed before the scheme's stated period ends.
Example: inside 90 days, 1% at NAV ₹100 gives ₹99 per unit; after 90 days you get the full ₹100.
Check the purchase date of each lot on your statement; a small deduction on redemption may be STT (0.001%).
Sources: Edelweiss Flexi Cap Fund Direct Growth (INDmoney); Fee Explainer – Exit load, STT.

question: I withdrew from the liquid fund 3 days after investing — why is the amount slightly lower than expected?
expected_facts: Liquid fund graded exit load on day 3 is 0.0060%
expected_fee_points: graded exit load applies to liquid funds for redemptions in the first 6 days (SEBI circular, Sep 2019)
load is a % of redemption proceeds and falls each day
worked example: ₹1,00,000 redeemed on day 3 → ₹6 exit load
premise_check: The INDmoney summary shows the liquid fund exit load as 0.0%; the factsheet's graded slabs override it for redemptions in the first week.
reference_answer: Redeeming on day 3 triggers the liquid fund's graded exit load of 0.0060% of redemption proceeds.
Factsheet slabs: day 1 0.0070%, falling 0.0005% a day to 0.0045% on day 6; nil from day 7.
SEBI requires liquid funds to charge this small graded exit load on redemptions within the first 7 days.
Example: redeeming ₹1,00,000 on day 3 costs ₹6, so you receive ₹99,994.
Check your purchase and redemption dates on the statement to confirm the day count.
Sources: Edelweiss Liquid Fund factsheet; SEBI circular SEBI/HO/IMD/DF2/CIR/P/2019/101; Fee Explainer – Graded exit load.

question: What is the expense ratio of the Index fund and does it get deducted from my account separately?
expected_facts: Nifty 50 Index fund expense ratio is 0.14% (direct plan)
expected_fee_points: TER is an annual % but is deducted daily from the fund's assets
it is reflected in the NAV, not debited separately from the investor's account

evidence.text: The TER is not charged separately to your bank account
It is deducted from the fund's Net Asset Value (NAV) on a daily basis.

reference_answer: The Edelweiss Nifty 50 Index Fund (Direct Growth) has an expense ratio of 0.14%, and it is not debited separately.
Scheme page: expense ratio 0.14% a year for the direct growth plan.
The TER is quoted yearly but deducted from fund assets every day, so it is already reflected in the NAV.
Example: on an average holding of ₹1,00,000, 0.14% is about ₹140 over a year, seen only as a lower NAV.
Check the latest factsheet for the current TER; it can change month to month.
Sources: Edelweiss Nifty 50 Index Fund Direct Growth (INDmoney); Fee Explainer – Expense ratio (TER).

question: My ₹10,000 SIP in the Large Cap fund showed ₹9,999.50 invested. What is the minimum SIP and why the difference?
expected_fee_points: stamp duty of 0.005% applies on every purchase, including SIP instalments

evidence.text: On a ₹10,000 SIP instalment, stamp duty is ₹0.50

open_issue: ET Money lists a ₹500 minimum SIP for this scheme; INDmoney (F-LC-01) shows ₹100. Confirm against the AMC KIM before the final eval run (see data/corpus/README.md).
reference_answer: The Large Cap fund's minimum SIP is ₹100; the ₹0.50 difference is stamp duty on your SIP instalment.
Scheme page: minimum lump sum ₹100 and minimum SIP ₹100 for the direct growth plan.
Stamp duty of 0.005% applies to every mutual fund purchase, including each SIP instalment, and is deducted before units are allotted.
Example: ₹10,000 × 0.005% = ₹0.50, so units are allotted for ₹9,999.50.
Check each SIP instalment on your statement; the same small deduction appears on every purchase.
Sources: Edelweiss Large Cap Fund Direct Growth (INDmoney); Fee Explainer – Stamp duty.
